evidence: High purity conductive Ag thin films with a low sheet resistance of 0.9 /sq (resistivity: 10-5 Ωcm) were deposited at 100°C and were characterized by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, optical transmittance and Rutherford back scattering techniques. The complex crystallizes in a triclinic crystal system, with the space group P1. The monomeric structure is retained in the solid crystalline form, while two individual molecules of [(NHC)Ag(hmds)] are present in the unit cell. The thermal properties of [(NHC)Ag(hmds)], which are highly relevant for ALD were investigated employing thermogravimetric (TG) and differential thermal analysis (DTA). The deposition of silver is indicated by two distinct contributions from Ag3d3/2 and Ag3d5/2 in the Ag3d core spectrum. The synthetic strategy (Scheme 1) for the formation of the new silver precursor was adapted from the analogous NHC-based copper(I) amides reported in the literature. Starting with the corresponding imidazolium chloride salt, deprotonation and salt metathesis with AgCl is achieved in-situ with two equivalents of lithium hexamethyldisilazide in tetrahydrofuran (THF) at 0 °C. To confirm the successful synthesis and the spectroscopic purity of the target compound [(NHC)Ag(hmds)], 1H and 13C NMR spectroscopy was performed in benzene-d6. Mass spectrometric analysis was performed to gain insight into the possible fragmentation pathways of [(NHC)Ag(hmds)] under EI-MS conditions in the gas-phase. The thermal properties of [(NHC)Ag(hmds)], which are highly relevant for ALD were investigated employing thermogravimetric (TG) and differential thermal analysis (DTA).
